prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One finished landscape 3:2 full-bleed picture-book illustration, one coherent scene and moment, no panels or contact sheet. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. The ONLY named human protagonist is Kit. Zoe MUST NOT appear. Ignore every other child shown in reference sheets; unnamed adults may appear only when this scene explicitly requires them. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Stop the Drum; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: Kit sits beside a single small drum secured on a low stand in a quiet bright music corner. The drum is open at the bottom, with one taut synthetic pale drumhead.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): One plain red cylindrical drum, cream taut drumhead and navy rim, fixed securely on a low navy stand; Kit uses his right palm to tap or rest on the head; no stick, mallet, second drum or floating hand; Small curved motion marks represent quick movement; they are diagrams, never cracks or extra drum skins
 Input references lock identity, prop design and location; compose a NEW image for the exact scene, never reproduce the reference-board layout. The reference and overall prop list may contain finished objects and later story events: these are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY, not permission to show them now. Show only the people, objects and development stage required below.
Page 5. Printed prose (NOT text to put in art): The top stops moving.
Required illustration: Close-up of the same flat head beneath Kit’s resting palm. No motion marks, arrows, cracked skin or duplicated fingers. The rim and stand remain identical.
Exact current state: Drumhead damped; right palm stationary on top.
Do not add later events, duplicate props or a separate inset. No written title; the app renders live text.
Production finish: every surface must be perfectly flat, clean digital cel color with smooth crisp outlines. ZERO paper grain, speckling, stipple, dither, paint, canvas fibers, mottling, scuffs or noisy gradients anywhere, including skin, rug, walls, table, floor and shadows. Prefer solid flat fills; any small shadow is one smooth flat shape. This is polished vector-like raster art, never a textured watercolor print. Do not include the reference-board framed music-note decoration or any written musical notes in the room.
HAND CONTINUITY CORRECTION. Use the LAST attached page7 drawing as pose authority: Kit's RIGHT arm is the NEAR arm emerging from the shoulder on the LEFT side of the picture, crossing in front of his torso toward drum. RIGHT hand rests FLAT with all fingers touching taut head, not lifted. His LEFT hand rests on his far knee, just as attached. Do not use the far arm from the shoulder on the right of picture to touch drum. REMOVE ALL motion and sound arcs: this page shows the resting/damping state. Same one drum and stand. Camera is a TIGHT close-up of right palm and drumhead, with only forearm and a little torso visible, no whole child needed.

visualReview.note: Directly viewed repaired native. Tight close-up of same resting right palm and taut cream head; no motion marks, cracks, duplicate fingers or deep dent, navy rim and drum retained.
